en: The blue-gray winged steed beneath me
Came to me from the unseen.
In Zhelpinish's lonely desert,
In that lonely desert he was found.
God sent him and made him a bird;
By God's decree, the winged steed
Was brought to your Bakay.
When I looked at the blue-gray winged steed,
Wishing the animal well,
His broad croup was a fathom wide,
A noble horse to ride into conflict.
Taking a red spear in hand,
He was a mount to ride into slaughter.
Ridden on reconnaissance, he never tired;
He had the bearing of a winged steed.
Thus my honor was safeguarded,
A winged steed found from the unseen.
Unable to remain in Zhelpinish,
Of the seven great peoples,
Unable to learn where they had gone,
I bound on my pine-shafted spear.
Against how many lands I waged war!
Breaking champions, I seized the ridges;
I seized the land stretching far and wide.
Attacking those around me,
I devastated the Kyzylbash people.
Finding no lion like you, my mighty one,
I tormented my damned soul.
I began havoc against those who assailed me.
At the earth's far end, Zhelpinish,
I left the land of Zhelpinish.
Finding no mountain to fling myself against,
Finding no enemy to fight,
The world's four corners
I traveled and circled four times,
Girded with an unsheathed sword.
In the desert of Mediyan,
I stalked and shot six geese.
With the wandering saint named Khizir
I lay down together.
At the middle of the night
A saintly person came,
An old man of sacred power came.
These are the words Bakay tells.
When I looked attentively,
It was the saintly old man himself;
As a father to me,
He had come to bestow his blessing.
My own father was Bay.
In the hands of the unbelievers,
Driven into exile, he had died.
There are more words I can tell.
Called by the name of Bay,
There is a city of my father.
Our ancestor was Karakan;
Warrior Karakan had died.
Coming out of China, Khan Molto
Had divided Karakan's eight sons,
Measuring them against a whip.
When I was six months old,
My unfortunate mother had died.
When I had reached one year,
My father had passed away.
‘If this child lives and does not die,
May he be a leader for the Muslims,’ he said;
His wish was fulfilled.
When my father Bay died,
The blessed saintly old man
To the earth's far end, Zhelpinish,
Had taken me away to Zhelpinish.
When I went to Zhelpinish,
I matured and became a warrior.
I became equal to warriors' sons;
From a little child I grew great.
When I reached seventeen,
In a dream as I slept,
The Creator put me to trouble.
Running up beside me came
A white-bearded wandering saint.
The saint spoke these words,
Words that put sorrow in my breast:
‘O warrior Bakay, listen:
You have a champion, a close support.
To become your companion,
You have champion Manas, your lion.
He is the champion, he is the support;
Born greater than mortals,
Champion Manas is that lion.
If at last you find Manas,
Listen willingly, my Bakay:
He will not saddle-sore your blue-gray steed,
He will never hurt your heart.
For keeping watch each day,
He is a ridge with a lofty back.
If you settle your camp by Manas,
He has all abundance at his command.
The youngest of the six lions,
God's beloved servant,
If you look within him,
He is broader than the face of the earth.
Go to Manas and you will prosper;
Playing knucklebones, you will rejoice.
When bored, you will hunt roe deer.
If you settle your camp by Manas,
You will live playing freely.
He is the lion to resolve your difficulties;
He is the warrior to relieve your pent-up sorrow.
If you climb upward, he is your support;
If you move downward, this Manas
Is your prop, my Bakay.
He is the accomplished one, he is the lion;
Making the whole earth submit,
He is the warrior to rule it alone.
Named Manas, an exceptional lion,
If you believe my words,
If you find Manas,
He will become your faithful companion.
The enemy on your right
He is the servant who will destroy;
The Chinese on your flank
He is the son who will slaughter.
These are the words I tell you.
To your magnanimous lion Manas
Become a companion yourself.
He is the Night of Power, he is the lion;
Who will brighten your brow,
He is the warrior who gathers treasure.
If Manas comes to you, you will prosper;
Becoming renowned warrior Bakay,
You will rejoice in ruling the world.
He is the warrior to understand your difficulties;
He is the wolf who will welcome you.
When you come into his hands,
From the spring before him
He will ride down to water his horse.
Giving you the name Khan Bakay,
He will make your name known to the world.
With a golden collar, proof against bullets,
Three times he will shake it out and put it on.
When you come into his hands,
He will contend with the whole wide world.
Find Manas and you will prosper;
Find the warrior and you will rejoice.
He is the wolf whose ambition will grow;
He is the warrior to undo your misfortune.
My dear Bakay, you yourself
Must find that Manas.
If you ask about Manas,
A dark wolf-man, a leopard,
With a hanging belly, a great paunch,
He has all abundance at his command.
Oceanlike Bakay, seek him and find him;
He is the lion to gladden your heart.
If you see inside Manas,
He is broader than the face of the earth.
The youngest of the six lions,
God's beloved servant,
He is magnanimous Manas the lion.
If you take him as a companion, mighty Bakay,
He is the lion who will understand your ways.
No mortal can approach him face to face;
Champion Manas the wolf-man
No mortal can force to bow.
When you go to Manas,
With double mail, its rings like larks' eyes,
He will put on a bulletproof coat.
Not merely the Chinese, but whole peoples,
If your mighty one comes into your hands,
He will contend with the world.
Make your home in Keng-Kol and Talas.
Make your support at your side
Jakyp's only son Manas.
He is a sheltering ridge, a refuge for nests.
Search out and find Manas;
He is the warrior who will ease your grief.
Your rendezvous companion when you scout,
If you find Manas,
Your companion until Judgment Day.
Now going to Altay,
Among your few Kyrgyz people
Manas was born there.
Herds of horses were slaughtered for his feast;
Then the name of Manas
Was given as the Greatest Madcap.
When he reached twelve years old,
By blood-stained champion Manas
Any mortal who assailed him was slaughtered.
When he reached twelve,
He began to rage fiercely.
Hearing news of Manas,
Esenkan, khan of Kakan,
Became utterly distraught.
With his mighty champions diminished,
With his envoys left stranded,
He began a monstrous quarrel.
All his giants and mighty men,
The scouts in between,
His envoys who came to Altay,
He utterly slaughtered them all.
That Manas was a warrior
Had become apparent, I heard.
Warriors died, the people were ruined;
Hero Manas the leopard
From the Kalmyks in Altay
Had separated, I heard.
Coming to take Manas captive,
He squandered his own wealth, they say.
Having all his monks slaughtered,
The Kalmyk warrior Zholoy
Fled back into Kakan, they say.
His fame is formidable, his wrath fierce;
He is the champion, he is the support.
If you seek out and find Manas,
He is the lion to bind about your waist.
If you go and find Manas,
For the whole wide world
He is the warrior who will be a pillar.
Seek and find him: your confidant.
If you find Manas,
He is your companion close to your soul.
His valor is proven among the people.
If you find Manas,
For you yourself, Bakay,
He will be your unfailing kinsman and support.
He will understand your words first;
He will hold you as his own one,
He will listen carefully to your words.
My Bakay, if you find Manas,
He will regard you as a prophet.
He will listen attentively to your words.
If you find Manas,
He will regard you as a saint.
Your Manas is no mere Manas: he is the Night of Power.
Take heed, Bakay, understand my words.
He will make your heart joyful and at ease.
If you find Manas,
He will make you khan over the wide world.
If somehow you find Manas,
Two reins and one lead rope
You will now take into your hands.
Among all the world's peoples
You will go as “Khan Bakay.”
A patterned chest, ten carpets,
My fierce one, if you find a soul companion,
I know Manas's circumstances.
An inlaid chest, forty carpets,
Do not suffer, leopard Bakay;
I know the mighty one's circumstances.
No enemy can tread across him;
He is a ridge with a precious steep path.
If you welcome Manas,
He is the lion who will release your laughter.
He was born in Altay.
His golden-wombed mother
Had a pregnancy craving for lion,
The mother who bore Manas.
